name: Salem Ghosts
description: A self-guided walking tour of documented 1692 witch trial history and the ghost legends attached to downtown Salem.

stops.name: Salem Common

viewpoint.description: Public sidewalk on the east side of Salem Common, beside the flagpole.

stops.narration: You are standing on the public sidewalk on the east side of Salem Common, beside the flagpole that has marked the center of the town since the 1600s. The Common was the muster field for the militia, and in 1692 the town's soldiers trained here before heading out to interrogations. The documented history of the Common as the town's training ground and public space is real. The legends about the Common, about soldiers returning from interrogations and about what was seen in the fog after dark, are part of Salem's storytelling tradition. The walker stands on the public sidewalk, and the Common's history is the spine. The documented history here is clear and well sourced, and the stories that surround it are folklore, told by visitors and by the people who live nearby. The walker who pauses on the public sidewalk can take in both layers at once, the record and the legend, and can leave knowing which is which.

stops.name: Witch House (outside)

viewpoint.description: Public sidewalk on Essex Street in front of the Witch House, across the street from the iron fence.

stops.narration: You are standing on the public sidewalk on Essex Street in front of the Witch House, across the street from the iron fence. The Witch House was the home of Judge Jonathan Corwin, one of the magistrates who presided over the 1692 witch trials. The documented history of Judge Corwin and the trials is real and well recorded, including his own letters and the court records. The stories that the Witch House is haunted are local legend, passed on by guides who say they see figures in the windows at night. The walker stands on the public sidewalk, and the house stays across the street beyond the fence, where the documented history is the only evidence. The documented history here is clear and well sourced, and the stories that surround it are folklore, told by visitors and by the people who live nearby. The walker who pauses on the public sidewalk can take in both layers at once, the record and the legend, and can leave knowing which is which.

The legends about ghosts walking among the gravestones are local folklore, passed on by visitors who say they see figures after dark. The walker stands on the public sidewalk, and the cemetery stays behind its gate. The documented history here is clear and well sourced, and the stories that surround it are folklore, told by visitors and by the people who live nearby. stops.name: Joshua Ward House

viewpoint.description: Public sidewalk on Essex Street in front of the Joshua Ward House, beside the doorway.

stops.narration: You are standing on the public sidewalk on Essex Street in front of the Joshua Ward House, beside the doorway. The house was built in 1800 on the site where Deputy Governor John Willard was imprisoned during the 1692 witch trials, and where he died under questionable conditions. The documented history of Willard's imprisonment and death is real, and the story of his cries from the jail are part of the trial record. The legend that the house is haunted by Willard's spirit is local folklore, passed on by guides who say they hear footsteps and see shadows. The walker stands on the public sidewalk, and the house stays across the street beyond the fence. The documented history here is clear and well sourced, and the stories that surround it are folklore, told by visitors and by the people who live nearby. The walker who pauses on the public sidewalk can take in both layers at once, the record and the legend, and can leave knowing which is which.
